topics.topic: Failure contract when runtime-settings reload finds missing or invalid configuration after startup
questions: If the environment becomes missing or invalid after startup and `load_runtime_settings` fails during a binary read, which typed failure and HTTP response must the caller receive, and does the failure cover an invalid unrelated runtime-setting row as well?
After a successful start, what exact failure must a Registry call return if reloading settings finds `REGISTRY_BASE_URL` missing, empty, whitespace-only or otherwise invalid as a runtime setting?

quotes:
The emitted `binary_storage`
  takes the storage root and the read limit the same way, from the
  `binary_storage_root` and `binary_max_read_bytes` fields of the settings
  `load_runtime_settings` returns, which it calls at each binary read, and
  refuses that read as `BinaryStorageError` when the settings cannot be
  loaded (owner 2026-11-09; `binary_storage_backend` schema version 2).

read_expense_document: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST translate a BinaryStorageError raised by read_binary into BinaryAccessRejected; it owns no transaction guard, because the only transaction is the one _authorize_document_reference opens and closes.

`PhotoValidationError` for a missing, another project's or an invisible
photo; `BinaryStorageError` for an unreadable object. Unlike documents, the
accepted service does not fold these into one answer.

_registry_url: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST join only the supplied relative path to the Registry deployment URL, which is the registry_base_url field of the RuntimeSettings that the imported load_runtime_settings returns when this function calls it, and MUST preserve that URL's own path prefix so a Registry deployed under a prefix keeps it on every request; it MUST NOT read the process environment itself. A missing or empty URL never reaches this function, because load_runtime_settings refuses the service start for it, and this function MUST NOT catch, translate or repair a refusal of load_runtime_settings. Each of the following MUST raise RegistryBoundaryError carrying the TRANSPORT_ERROR member of = models.RegistryFailureKind, never a raw ValueError or other untyped error, and never a repaired URL: the URL is not a usable http or https base URL; it carries userinfo credentials, which are rejected rather than stripped, retained, or forwarded; the supplied path is absolute or protocol-relative, which MUST NOT be allowed to replace the host or scheme.

Any other failure is 500. No failure becomes a success, an empty list or a
  zero, except in the two reads whose Errors say so:
  `derived_views.build_project_overview` turns a part's failure into that
  part's availability, and `derived_views.list_viewer_projects` leaves out a
  project whose Registry context fails.
judgement.why: Later module, note, and API texts require every failed binary-settings reload to become BinaryStorageError, concealed as BinaryAccessRejected for documents and exposed for photos, while a Registry settings-load refusal is neither cached nor translated and therefore follows the generic 500 mapping.

The passage must either remove `rules.exception_payload_policy` from the specification and retain the policy only as a design fact, or give the value one of the standard's valid paths to generated code.

topics.topic: BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT requirement and startup path-validation rules
questions: Is `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT` required, and exactly which empty, whitespace, relative, nonexistent, non-directory, unreadable, or unsafe path values stop startup?

quotes:
The portal runs as one service with one SQLite database file and one local
directory under which `file_ref` resolves to stored bytes; the binary read
bound `binary_max_read_bytes` stays a deployment setting. The service is
configured only by environment variables, which it validates when it starts
(the Registry address among them since the owner's decision of 2026-11-09:
its absence stops the start, State 2 A30), and answers only on the trusted hosts it is
configured with; wildcard hosts and origins are refused.

- `binary_read_limit_env_name`: the binary read limit is the environment
  variable `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES`, a required row of the start-up table read
  into the `binary_max_read_bytes` field of `RuntimeSettings`; the storage
  root `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT` likewise into `binary_storage_root`. The emitted
  `binary_storage` takes both from the settings `load_runtime_settings`
  returns, which it calls at each read, as its backend IR
  (`binary_storage_backend` schema version 2, `settings`) names them, and
  reads no environment itself (owner 2026-11-09, SPEC_STANDARD 6.11;
  Factory code-factory #201). Until then it read both variables itself
  (Factory `a6916180314d`). No model-written module reads them.

- CFG-002: a required start-up variable that is missing or invalid stops
  the start before any request is served; for the Registry URL the start-up
  check refuses only a missing, empty or whitespace-only value, and any other unusable URL
  fails each Registry call as `transport_error` (A6).
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT as a required, startup-validated safe directory and refuses whitespace, relative, nonexistent, non-directory, unreadable, or unsafe values before serving; another merely loads the supplied string and defers some or all failures to the first binary read, which the deployment operator and binary client observe.
judgement.why: The texts place BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT in RuntimeSettings and generally reject invalid required rows, but do not state its requiredness or the exact startup-valid path set.

table `config.runtime_environment_variables` into `RuntimeSettings` at each
call of `load_runtime_settings` — once at start by `runtime` and by the
bootstrap command, and again at each Registry call by `registry_gateway`
and at each binary read by the emitted `binary_storage` (owner 2026-11-09)
— including the startup consistency of the binary bounds (A14). Factory
`38626cc7be12`.

  takes the storage root and the read limit the same way, from the
  `binary_storage_root` and `binary_max_read_bytes` fields of the settings

  refuses that read as `BinaryStorageError` when the settings cannot be

topics.topic: Whether refused catalog actions create rejected audit records
questions: Does a refused occurrence of a catalog action write exactly one rejected audit record, or do refused operations other than snapshot import and failed login write no record?

quotes:
One audit record per action occurrence; `staff.recovery_override` carries
enhanced detail via its entity reference: its record is the distinct
action `staff.recovery_override` naming the account (`entity_id` = its
`staff_id`) and the acting administrator; neither the replaced nor the
replacement email is kept in any record, and the account's current email
is the only evidence of the change (Factory code
`application/staff_identity.py` `perform_recovery_override`; Owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated.)

Every other refused operation
rolls its transaction back and writes no record. The closed set of
`reason_code` values is therefore the seven `ImportRejectReason` values and
`integrity_conflict`.
judgement.why: Both questioned audit passages are unchanged in the closed and current State 2 texts, and the A13 changes only annotate and retire old rules namespaces without changing refusal auditing.
